auxiliary_tla_invariants.TypeOK: The type invariant of each module. TLC checks it in every configuration. It is not a property of the substrate.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.IndInv: The inductive strengthening of T3 and T4 (CheckpointReplay) for the Apalache BASE and STEP checks. TLC checks it on every reachable state of the two safe CheckpointReplay configurations.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.LockIndInv: The inductive strengthening of T5 (TxnLockCoverage) for the Apalache BASE and STEP checks. TLC checks it on every reachable state of MC_TxnLockCoverage.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.CommitOrderWitness: When the ghost serialOk holds, the commit order itself witnesses T5. TLC checks it on every reachable state of MC_TxnLockCoverage.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.HeadIndInv: The inductive strengthening of U1-U3 and U9-U12 (HeadOnlyDiscipline) for the Apalache BASE and STEP checks: the ords and the carried ords are below the counter and unique, the carried ords differ from the stored ords, the elements in flight have their shapes, and the history flags hold. TLC checks it on every reachable state of MC_HeadOnlyDiscipline and MC_HeadOnlyDiscipline_Reissue.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.HandleIndInv: The inductive strengthening of U5-U8 (NativeHandles) for the Apalache BASE and STEP checks: live spaces are durable, only live spaces have collection counters, and no counter or log grows faster than the steps. TLC checks it on every reachable state of MC_NativeHandles.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.SharedQueueRaces: CounterConflict: two branches that use one queue race in check #1. It restates the Rocq headlines Q21, Q22 and Q24, which their own property tests cover. TLC checks it in MC_CounterConflict. With stacks, MC_CounterConflict_Stacks checks it too, and it restates the P5 headline shared_collection_race (R63).
auxiliary_tla_invariants.FirstOpsRace: CounterConflict: two branches that open queues of one space race on S(sid). It restates the Rocq headline Q23, which its own property test covers. TLC checks it in MC_CounterConflict. With stacks, MC_CounterConflict_Stacks checks it too, and it restates the P5 headline shared_collection_race (R63).
auxiliary_tla_invariants.OutcomeTypeOK: The type invariant of OutcomeSpec of NativeReplay.tla. TLC checks it in its configurations. It is not a property of the backend.
auxiliary_tla_invariants.ScheduleTypeOK: The type invariant of ScheduleSpec of NativeReplay.tla. TLC checks it in its configurations. It is not a property of the backend.

Q1.name: kind_byte_injective
Q1.statement: The KIND byte names its kind and durability: two (kind, durability) pairs with one byte are equal.

Q2.name: storage_id_injective
Q2.statement: The storage ids (data, path index, counters, allocator) are injective in their space, kind and key.

Q3.name: handle_id_injective
Q3.statement: The handle id E0‖H‖sid names exactly one native space.

Q4.name: ephemeral_durable_disjoint
Q4.statement: No ephemeral id equals a durable id.

Q5.name: reified_ids_disjoint_from_new_ids
Q5.statement: No Reified id equals the 32-byte id of a name that new makes.

Q6.name: reified_ids_disjoint_from_byte_names_and_mettail
Q6.statement: No Reified id equals a 1-byte system name or a MeTTaTron id.

Q7.name: op_ids_pairwise_distinct
Q7.statement: The op ids [E0, op] of the factories, the system processes and the markers are pairwise distinct.

Q8.name: decode_encode_reified_id
Q8.statement: decode_reified_id inverts every constructor, and it accepts only their images.

Q9.name: space_and_collection_counters_distinct
Q9.statement: The space counter S(sid) differs from every collection counter S(sid,k).

Q10.name: name_id_routes_to_sid
Q10.statement: A name id N(sid‖tail) decodes to its space.

Q11.name: canon_respects_par_eq
Q11.statement: Channels that are equal as Par values have one canonical key.

Q12.name: datum_unwrap_wrap
Q12.statement: Unwrapping a wrapped datum gives the order and the payload back.

Q13.name: datum_wrap_injective
Q13.statement: The datum envelope is injective in the order and the payload.

Q14.name: datum_unwrap_sound
Q14.statement: The datum decoder accepts only the image of the encoder.

Q15.name: continuation_unwrap_wrap
Q15.statement: Unwrapping a wrapped continuation gives the order and the body back.

Q16.name: counter_and_config_roundtrip
Q16.statement: The counter and config records round-trip, the config as its canonical map (I-17).

Q17.name: envelope_kinds_disjoint
Q17.statement: The tags D, K, S and C are pairwise distinct, so no record decodes as another kind.

Q18.name: no_reified_datum_is_single_number
Q18.statement: No Reified datum is a single number, so the merger never treats one as a number channel.

Q19.name: unknown_version_rejected
Q19.statement: A tag with another version or kind byte is rejected.

Q20.name: check1_race_iff
Q20.statement: The restatement of HEAD check #1: a race exactly for a shared non-persistent IO event that is not mergeable in both logs.

Q21.name: ordered_writes_race_on_counter
Q21.statement: Two branches that write one queue race on its counter S(sid,k).

Q22.name: ordered_reads_race_on_counter
Q22.statement: A peek bumps the counter too, so two branches that read one queue race (A2).

Q23.name: first_ops_race_on_space_counter
Q23.statement: Two branches whose first operations open collections of one space race on S(sid) (A25).

Q24.name: crossed_collections_race
Q24.statement: Branches that use two queues in crossed orders race on both counters.

Q25.name: same_block_ops_chain
Q25.statement: Two deploys of one block that use one queue form one chain (depends).

Q26.name: unordered_writes_commute
Q26.statement: Writes to a bag need no counter: they never race, and the merge holds both serial orders.

Q27.name: merge_without_race_is_serializable
Q27.statement: Without a check #1 race, the merged state and the observations are those of a serial run.

Q28.name: counter_free_peek_admits_write_skew
Q28.statement: A peek without the counter admits the peek/dequeue write skew (computed counterexample).

Q29.name: queue_head_is_min_ord
Q29.statement: The head of each side has the least (ord, bytes).

Q30.name: queue_produce_preserves_inv
Q30.statement: A produce keeps INV: no pending match between the heads.

Q33.name: queue_head_blocks
Q33.statement: A head that does not match blocks the entries behind it.

Q34.name: queue_loop_bounded_or_reissues
Q34.statement: A plan stages at most FIRE_ROUND_CAP fires, at most one more than the queue length, or it re-issues.

Q35.name: queue_ord_fresh
Q35.statement: The ord of an operation is new in its collection.

Q36.name: queue_plan_permutation_invariant
Q36.statement: The plan ignores the list order of the staged view.

Q37.name: legacy_scan_violates_head_blocks
Q37.statement: The legacy waiter scan breaks head-only matching (computed example).

Q38.name: classify_space_ref_total_deterministic
Q38.statement: Every space reference meets exactly one of the five rules of classify_space_ref.

Q39.name: handle_requires_write_flag
Q39.statement: A reference names a native space only as a bare handle or a writable bundle of one.

Q40.name: reified_non_handle_not_a_space_ref
Q40.statement: A Reified id that is not a handle is NotASpaceRef, never an agent.

Q41.name: route_total_deterministic
Q41.statement: A route fails only on the key, and it depends on the context only through its native space.

Q42.name: route_rules
Q42.statement: The routing rules R1 to R5.

Q43.name: space_name_route_ignores_ctx
Q43.statement: A space name routes to its own space under every context.

Q44.name: r7_route_ignores_ctx
Q44.statement: The R7 backend agrees with the reducer on every channel that is not forged.

Q45.name: ordinary_channels_route_default
Q45.statement: The channels of an ordinary program route to the default space, and the fast path is exact.

Q46.name: use_wrapper_restores_ctx
Q46.statement: A body that the reducer stores under a context runs in that context when it fires.

Q47.name: handle_dispatch_total
Q47.statement: The handle process drops a call on a non-handle, aborts on a dangling handle, and replies only on a reply name.

Q48.name: family_index_bijective
Q48.statement: The 32 families have the indices 0 to 31, one each, so no two share a factory channel or a capability.

Q49.name: aliases_map_to_family
Q49.statement: The URNs and the FIPS aliases parse to their families, and a config names its family.

Q50.name: qualifier_matrix
Q50.statement: HashSet takes only seq, and P4 creates only default (durable) spaces.

Q51.name: constructor_parse_canonical
Q51.statement: Every canonical constructor parses back from its elements.

Q52.name: constructor_parse_sound
Q52.statement: The constructor parser accepts only the canonical sequence [q?][FREE?][PARAMS?].

Q53.name: sid_derivation_deterministic
Q53.statement: The sid is the 32-byte SpaceId draw of the random state of the call.

Q54.name: persistent_op_call_aborts
Q54.statement: A persistent send to an op that takes calls, or to a handle, aborts before the call (A21).

Q55.name: space_already_exists_is_deterministic_abort
Q55.statement: A creation over an existing C(sid) aborts in play and replay alike. A commit applies all three operations or none.

Q56.name: refresh_strict_decode_erase
Q56.statement: I-20: after the refresh, the strict decode is the decode of Encoding.v, and it accepts only derived flags.

Q57.name: connective_marker_tuple_recognized
Q57.statement: I-20: a canonical marker tuple with connective_used = true is recognized.

Q58.name: refreshed_decode_commutes_with_subst
Q58.statement: I-20: the refresh makes the strict decode of a substituted tuple commute with substitution.

Q59.name: operation_trace_covered
Q59.statement: Decision 42: every collection operation reserves each read and copy before it makes it (DR-88 prefix coverage), the reads of the outcome after the commit included.

Q60.name: reservations_precede_commit
Q60.statement: Decision 42: the work after the commit reserves nothing.

Q61.name: cut_rejects_before_commit
Q61.statement: Decision 42: a budget below the reservations of an operation is exceeded by a staged reservation, so the operation fails before the commit and has no effect.

Q62.name: scan_charge_permutation_invariant
Q62.statement: Decision 42: the charge of a head scan does not depend on the list order of its side.

Q63.name: operation_charge_permutation_invariant
Q63.statement: Decision 42: the charge of an operation does not depend on the list order of the staged view.

Q64.name: scan_charge_independent_of_unread_payloads
Q64.statement: Decision 42: the payloads of the entries that a scan does not copy do not change its charge.

Q65.name: p4_scan_covered_only_if_free
Q65.statement: Decision 42 (negative control): the P4 scan, which reserved nothing for its own decodes and copies, satisfies prefix coverage only when that work is zero.

Q66.name: unprepaid_trace_uncovered
Q66.statement: Decision 42 (negative control): without the prepaid reservations, the reads of the outcome after the commit break prefix coverage.

Q67.name: native_execution_runs_spaces
Q67.statement: Decision 47 (amends decision 46): native play runs a space entry as legacy execution runs it, and a native replay runtime that its environment bound runs it as native play, so play and replay stage the same operations; a native replay runtime that is not bound yet, and a detached runtime, stage nothing and fail with RuntimeUnavailable.

Q68.name: persistent_reentry_never_spent
Q68.statement: Decision 43: a re-entry never spends a persistent element. It re-issues again, or it ends stored or parked at its place.

Q69.name: queue_reissue_keeps_ord
Q69.statement: Decision 43: a re-issued persistent element keeps the ord of its first round. Its round bumps the counter by one and keeps wf'.

Q70.name: queue_reentry_preserves_shadow_inv
Q70.statement: Decision 43: every fresh operation and every re-entry keeps wf' and SHADOW.

Q71.name: queue_quiescent_inv
Q71.statement: Decision 43: SHADOW with nothing in flight is INV. Every run of rounds keeps wf' and SHADOW, and it has INV whenever nothing is in flight.

Q72.name: queue_fifo_with_reentries
Q72.statement: Decision 43: over runs with re-entries, the records that are not persistent leave in increasing ord, each older than every such record that stays.

Q73.name: queue_head_blocks_reentry
Q73.statement: Decision 43: a re-entry behind an older head of its side rests at its place and fires nothing. A re-entry at the head that does not match the other head rests too. A fire meets the head of the other side.

Q74.name: queue_reentry_loop_bounded_or_reissues
Q74.statement: Decision 43: a re-entry stages at most FIRE_ROUND_CAP fires. A re-issue carries the first-round ord exactly for a persistent element.

Q75.name: queue_reentry_permutation_invariant
Q75.statement: Decision 43: a re-entry depends on the entries of the collection, not on their list order.

Q76.name: fresh_ord_reissue_loses_first_round_place
Q76.statement: Decision 43 (negative control C0): with a fresh ord, a re-issued persistent element rests behind a younger record and loses its first-round place.

Q77.name: nonpersistent_first_ord_reentry_breaks_quiescent_inv
Q77.statement: Decision 43 (negative control C1): an element that is not persistent and keeps its first-round ord leaves a pending match with nothing in flight.

U1.name: QuiescentNoPendingMatch
U1.statement: With no element in flight, the head record and the head waiter never match (INV), on every schedule (decision 43).

U2.name: HeadBlocks
U2.statement: Every fire involves the head of the other side, on every schedule.

U3.name: FifoOrder
U3.statement: An element fires only when no entry of its own side precedes it, also after a re-entry (QD-7, QD-9).

U4.name: NoMergedOrderFabrication
U4.statement: A merge without a check #1 race is a serial run of the two branches.

U5.name: HandleUnique
U5.statement: One config record and one handle continuation for each created sid.

U6.name: DanglingIsDeterministicError
U6.statement: A handle call aborts with DanglingHandle exactly when its space has no config.

U7.name: DurableSurvivesRestart
U7.statement: Every durable space survives a checkpoint and a restart.

U8.name: HandleCallsMergeLikeContracts
U8.statement: Handle calls on disjoint collections merge like contract calls, and calls on one collection race.

U9.name: ShadowedNoPendingMatch
U9.statement: While an element is in flight, a matching pair of heads needs an element in flight that precedes the head of its side (SHADOW, decision 43).

U10.name: ReissueKeepsOrd
U10.statement: Every persistent element in flight carries the ord of its first round (decision 43).

U11.name: IntroducedOnce
U11.statement: Each persistent element takes a fresh ord exactly once, so its record and its introduction are the same in every round (decision 43).

U12.name: LeaveOrder
U12.statement: Records that are not persistent leave in increasing ord, each older than every such record that stays.

Q78.name: queue_restore_realizes_plan
Q78.statement: Decision 45 (Rule E): the staged operations of a plan, with the re-store after each peek fire of a record that is not persistent, give the records of the logical plan under the Rule E effects of the substrate, up to list order.

Q79.name: legacy_rebracket_eq_host
Q79.statement: Decision 45 (Option P): a space job that stages its operations through the legacy chain makes the legacy log of the host program of the same operations, with the same remaining budget, status and applied operations, for every charge rule, call acceptance and budget. The status names the stop point, and a stop at a pre-charge or a post-charge of operation i applies exactly the operations of the host program.

Q80.name: legacy_replay_stops_with_play
Q80.statement: Decision 45 (Option P): replay stages the operations of play and pairs each operation whose body play applied (decision 36). Then replay makes the legacy log, the remaining budget, the status and the applied operations of play, and it never diverges.

U13.name: LegacyChargesFollowHost
U13.statement: Decision 45 (Option P): in a legacy deploy, whenever play has no open transaction, play has the legacy log, the remaining budget and the stop point of the equivalent host program: the same host operations ran, and the deploy failed exactly when the program failed. A completed replay has the legacy state of that program.

P5.design: P5 design v3 (decision 48) and the W2 batch reports. R# are Rocq headlines and V# are TLA+ invariants. V1-V8 are the invariants of GenericRSpace.tla, V9-V10 the allocator invariants of CounterConflict.tla. The properties of the engine run the real bag, queue and cell disciplines and a probe of the set. witness_tests lists deterministic tests of the W2 code. The engine anchor prop_join_engine_agrees_with_drivers_without_joins covers the two search headlines, because on a join-free collection the engine must make the choices of the drivers.

R1.name: cell_capacity_one
R1.statement: The cell plans keep at most one record and one waiter. A plan fails with CellOccupied exactly when the same plan without the capacity check overflows a side, and otherwise the two plans are equal. This holds for every element of offer and receive, so for a fresh operation and, by headline 3, for a re-entered one.

R2.name: cell_restore_never_occupied
R2.statement: Every staged operation of a cell plan applies to the staged view at its point with the capacity check of Cx::check_capacity. In particular the re-store of Rule E meets an empty record slot, because the peek fire removed the record and the cell held one record.

R3.name: cell_reentry_as_fresh
R3.statement: A re-entered element with a valid first-round ord runs the plan of a fresh element with that ord on the bumped collection. So it keeps its record and its identity, it fires as a fresh element fires, and it fails with CellOccupied exactly when a fresh element would.

R4.name: fixed_array_allocates_at_most_size
R4.statement: A fixed Array of size s allocates at most s names, each index below s, and its key check accepts exactly the index names of the space below s.

R5.name: fixed_array_out_of_names_exact
R5.statement: A fixed Array fails with OutOfNames exactly when the next index plus the count exceeds its size, and then it allocates nothing and keeps its allocator.

R6.name: cyclic_array_index_mod_size
R6.statement: A cyclic Array of size s allocates the indices (n + i) mod s and keeps every index and its next value below s.

R7.name: allocation_batch_atomic
R7.statement: An allocation either fails with OutOfNames and changes nothing, or allocates exactly its count of indices with one take and one put of the allocator record.

R8.name: fixed_array_indices_sequential
R8.statement: A fixed Array allocates the indices 0, 1, 2 and onward in order, and each batch is the next run of consecutive indices.

R9.name: allocator_indices_distinct
R9.statement: Every store except a cyclic Array never allocates one index twice.

R10.name: allocator_identities_unique
R10.statement: The creation of the allocator record and every take and put of the allocations have distinct event identities.

R11.name: alloc_trace_covered
R11.statement: An allocation reserves every read before it makes it, reserves nothing after the commit, and reads exactly what it reserves (decision 42).

R12.name: vector_index_is_counter
R12.statement: A Vector allocates the indices 0, 1, 2 and onward without a size bound below its counter limit, and its key check accepts exactly the index names of the space.

R13.name: vector_gensym_distinct
R13.statement: A Vector never allocates one index twice.

R14.name: vector_gensym_monotonic
R14.statement: Each gensym of a Vector allocates the next index, so the indices grow by one with each call.

R15.name: hashmap_iteration_permutation_invariant
R15.statement: The records of each key and every order-free iteration of the HashMap store do not depend on the order of the puts.

R16.name: hashmap_get_put_other
R16.statement: A put or a take on one key leaves the records of every other key unchanged, and a put on a key adds its record to that key.

R17.name: query_source_routes_inner_channel
R17.statement: A receive whose source is a QUERY tuple reads from the inner channel of the query under the read rule of a receive source. The default space refuses a query with QuerySpecUnsupported, a user agent refuses it with QuerySpecUnsupportedOnAgentSpace (P8 step 3), and a QUERY tuple never becomes a host channel.

R18.name: registered_families_complete
R18.statement: A registered family has the URN of its family, the op of its index, the body ref 200 + op, arity 2, a constructor schema and a wired dispatch arm. A family is registered exactly when it has a row and an arm, and no two registered families share an op.

R19.name: aliases_bind_family_capability
R19.statement: The alias names the op of its family and is not the URN of the family. An alias is registered exactly when its family is registered. The URN map of the definitions is a function, the alias binds the op of its family, and so does the URN of the family: both bind the capability bundle+{[0xE0, op]}.

R20.name: constructor_params_validated
R20.statement: A family without a schema is unavailable. Positional params fail first. The first unknown key fails with the least (distance, key) suggestion within two edits, a deterministic function of the key and of the schema.

R21.name: priorities_validated
R21.statement: Exactly the priority queue families take the optional priorities, which no family requires. Its rule accepts exactly the GInt values in [1, i64_max], that is every GInt of at least 1, and the config keeps the canonical value. Without it the call is valid, and the levels have no bound.

R22.name: array_size_validated
R22.statement: Every Array family requires size and takes the optional cyclic, and every other family takes neither. size accepts exactly the GInt values in [1, i64_max], and cyclic exactly the GBool values. A call without size fails with MissingParam after the key check.

R23.name: prefix_key_iff_prefix
R23.statement: A prefix of a path is exactly a prefix key that is a byte prefix of the path key.

R24.name: reroot_ident
R24.statement: Re-rooting under the empty suffix gives the value itself.

R25.name: reroot_compose
R25.statement: Re-rooting composes. For a PathMap the composition of two re-rootings is the re-rooting under the joined suffix. For every other value the delivery on a shorter prefix prepends the extra suffix to the list of the delivery on the longer prefix.

R26.name: reroot_injective
R26.statement: Under a fixed suffix, re-rooting loses no logical information, and under a suffix that is not empty two values have equal deliveries exactly when they are logically equal.

R27.name: fips_example
R27.statement: The FIPS example. A send on @[0,1,2] is a send on every prefix. @[0,1,2]!({|"hi"|}), @[0,1,2]!({|"hello"|}) and @[0,1,3]!({|"there"|}) received on @[0,1] bind {|[2,"hi"]|}, {|[2,"hello"]|} and {|[3,"there"]|}. @[0,1,2]!(42) binds [2, 42], and @[0,1,2,"hi"]!({||}) binds {|[2,"hi"]|}.

R28.name: candidate_order_total
R28.statement: For every strict total order of the ranks, the candidate order is a strict total order, and the exact path comes first.

R29.name: bag_visit_order_canonical
R29.statement: The visit order of the records is sorted by source key, holds the records, and does not depend on the list order of the store.

R30.name: bag_consume_first_spatial_match
R30.statement: The receive fires the first record in canonical order that its pattern binds, when its guard admits it. No earlier record matches. The receive parks when nothing matches, or when the guard refuses the first match, whatever the later records (decision 37: the guard is checked once).

R31.name: bag_persistent_match_not_removed
R31.statement: A fire on a persistent record leaves it (a COMM never removes a persistent record).

R32.name: bag_multiplicity_preserved
R32.statement: For every record, a store adds exactly one occurrence, a fire removes exactly the one non-persistent record that it binds, and no other operation changes the records.

R33.name: bag_removal_keeps_equal_duplicate
R33.statement: Of two or more equal records, a fire removes exactly one and leaves the others.

R34.name: bag_peek_restore_is_host_second_send
R34.statement: A peek receive that settles stages exactly the host program: the fire, then the second send of the removed record, which is offered to the waiters first and registers the authority of the record. When no waiter takes the record, the record is stored again, so the peek leaves the multiset of records as it was.

R35.name: scan_trace_covered
R35.statement: Every prefix of the trace of a scan of the driver, the reads after the commit included, reads at most what it reserved (decision 42).

R36.name: waiter_removal_by_record_identity
R36.statement: In a side without duplicates (F14), the fire of [w] removes [w] and keeps every other waiter, whatever their patterns (D10).

R37.name: pattern_equality_removal_can_remove_another_waiter
R37.statement: Two waiters with equal patterns, with the other waiter [v] parked in front of the fired waiter [w]. The legacy removal keeps the fired waiter and removes [v], where the removal by identity removes [w].

R38.name: park_byte_identity_idempotent
R38.statement: An equal park changes nothing, a new waiter is added in front, and a side stays without duplicates.

R39.name: waiter_visit_order_canonical
R39.statement: The waiter order is sorted by key, holds the waiters, and does not depend on the list order of the store. A send fires the first waiter in that order that fits, so every earlier waiter fails its pattern or its guard (decision 37, the produce side).

R40.name: head_waiter_unique
R40.statement: A head-only side offers at most one candidate. It is the least waiter of the side, and a side with waiters offers one. A scan side offers every waiter.

R41.name: space_match_is_injected_match
R41.statement: The match of a plan is the injected match. 1. A fire of the scan driver or of the head driver binds the spatial match that the injected matcher computes, and the injected guard admitted it. The fired partner is a candidate of the plan. 2. A plan depends on the matcher only through its results. 3.

R42.name: guard_once_greedy_like_head
R42.statement: The guard is checked once, greedily, as the head driver checks it. 1. RECEIVE-SCAN chooses as the host consume: the first spatial match, then the guard once, and a refusal parks. 2. OFFER-SCAN chooses as the host produce: a guard refusal moves to the next waiter (the ids of one staged view are distinct). 3.

R43.name: wildcard_matcher_degenerate
R43.statement: The legacy WildcardMatch is the degenerate instance. A pattern for 42 receives 43 on the consume side and on the produce side, and the pattern plays no part in a choice. The real matcher parks and stores.

R44.name: consume_fires_only_matching
R44.statement: Every consume plan, of the scan driver and of the cell, stages only fires whose dispatched record is a stored record that matches the pattern spatially and whose binding the guard admitted.

R45.name: produce_fires_only_matching
R45.statement: Every produce plan, of the scan driver and of the cell, stages only fires whose waiter is stored, matches the datum spatially and admits the binding.

R46.name: unordered_no_pending_match
R46.statement: Bag, set and cell plans keep the rule of no pending match. Every produce, consume and re-entry of the scan driver keeps no_pending, every committed plan of the cell keeps cell_inv, and cell_inv implies no_pending.

R47.name: peek_restore_equals_host_reproduce
R47.statement: A peek of a non-persistent record stages the fire over the record and then exactly the plan of the second send of the host, with the bytes, the own authority and the identity of the record. The plain restore of a cell equals the second send of the cell.

R48.name: scan_reissue_identity_stable
R48.statement: Decision 43 for a collection without a counter (bag and set). 1. Every order is 0, and a re-issued order other than 0 is Inconsistent. 2. Every round of a re-issued scan produce stages the element of its first round: the same record bytes, persistence and authority, so the same produce identity. 3.

R49.name: engine_primitives_trace_covered
R49.statement: The staging primitives of the S1 engine reserve each read, copy and growth of the staged list before they make it, reserve nothing after the commit, and fail before the commit under a cut budget (decision 42).

V1.name: NoPendingMatch
V1.statement: After every step, no stored record and no stored waiter without a guard match each other in a bag, set or cell.

V2.name: PatternEnforcement
V2.statement: Every fire binds a record whose value the pattern of the waiter matches and whose guard admits it.

V3.name: Conservation
V3.statement: Every record that a send introduced is stored, delivered, re-stored after a peek, or in flight, so no record is lost or created.

V4.name: NoDoubleSpend
V4.statement: A non-persistent record is spent at most once: by one fire that does not peek, or by one retirement.

V5.name: AtomicReservation
V5.statement: A fire removes only records that are present in the view of its step, all of them in that step.

V6.name: SetClassRetired
V6.statement: After a consume or a send that fires a waiter of a set, no stored non-persistent member of the class of the fired value remains.

V7.name: CellCapacity
V7.statement: A cell holds at most one record and at most one waiter after every step.

V8.name: PeekRestoresRecord
V8.statement: Every stored record and every datum in flight carries its own introduction authority, and every store happens only when no waiter matches and admits the record.

V9.name: NoDuplicateIndex
V9.statement: When merge check #1 finds no race between two branches, the branches allocated disjoint index names of the space.

V10.name: AllocationsRace
V10.statement: Two branches that both allocate names of one space consume one allocator record, so merge check #1 reports a race.

R50.name: stack_head_is_max_ord
R50.statement: The top of each side is an entry of that side with the greatest (ord, rank), and a side has a top exactly when it is not empty.

R51.name: stack_produce_preserves_inv
R51.statement: A produce that completes in its round leaves INV: the top record and the top waiter do not match. The settle after the plan restores INV, so the produce needs no premise.

R52.name: stack_consume_preserves_inv
R52.statement: A consume that completes in its round leaves INV.

R53.name: stack_lifo
R53.statement: Every fire of an operation, of a settle job and of a re-entry binds the top waiter and the top record, and its incoming side is above every stored entry of its side (LifoOrder).

R54.name: stack_head_blocks
R54.statement: For a cap above 0, a top that does not match blocks: the produce stores the datum on top and the consume parks the continuation on top, with no fire, although an entry below the top may fit.

R55.name: stack_settle_terminates
R55.statement: A settle that starts after f fires of its transaction makes at most cap - f fires and at most mu fires, plus one fire for a divergent pair. A settle that stops at the cap brings its transaction to exactly cap fires, a divergent pair has a persistent waiter, and a settle that ends Quiescent leaves INV. Every transaction (a produce, a consume, a settle job and a re-entry) makes at most cap fires with its settles, and a transaction that re-issues at the cap made exactly cap fires (I-21).

R56.name: stack_plan_permutation_invariant
R56.statement: Two views with the same entries in other list orders stage the same operations in a produce, a consume and a settle job, take the same next round, and reach views with the same entries.

R57.name: stack_without_settle_breaks_inv
R57.statement: Without the settle, the computed counterexample of the P5 design v2, section 3.1 breaks INV at the end of a completed operation. With the settle after the plan, the stack lifts the exposed record, offers it again, and INV holds.

R58.name: stack_reentry_at_lifo_place
R58.statement: For a cap above 0, a re-issued persistent element below the younger top of its side is stored or parked at its LIFO place with no fire. Above the top, or on an empty side, it plans as a fresh element does, from the fire count of its transaction (decision 43).

R59.name: stack_reissue_keeps_ord
R59.statement: A re-issued operation carries the order of its first round exactly when it is persistent, every round bumps the counter once, and a re-entered datum stores only itself (decision 43).

R60.name: stack_peek_restore_needs_no_settle
R60.statement: For a cap above 0, a peek of a top record that is not persistent fires, removes the record and stores it again at its order before any settle step, so the settle after the plan stages nothing (decision 45, Rule E).

R61.name: settle_trace_covered
R61.statement: A settle reserves its reads before it makes them: its trace satisfies prefix coverage, the reads of the outcome after the commit included (decision 42, DR-88).

R62.name: stack_settle_keeps_unspent_records
R62.statement: From every fire count of the transaction, a stored record leaves the store during a settle only when a fire of a waiter that does not peek spends it, and then the record is not persistent (decisions 30 and 45).

V11.name: LifoOrder
V11.statement: Every fire binds the top of the other side, its incoming element has an ord at least the ord of every stored entry of its own side, and every lift takes the top record, on every schedule.

V12.name: StackNoPendingMatch
V12.statement: With no round in progress, no element in flight and no settle job, the top record and the top waiter do not match (INV), on every schedule.

V13.name: NoRecordLost
V13.statement: A record that was stored is stored, or in flight in the current settle, or a fire spent it, on every schedule.

V14.name: ReissueKeepsOrd
V14.statement: A re-issued persistent element carries the ord of its first round, and a re-issued element that is not persistent carries none, on every schedule (decision 43).

V15.name: TxnFiresBounded
V15.statement: No space transaction makes more than Cap fires, its settles included, on every schedule (revision I-21). The ghost txnFires counts every fire of the round, also the last fire of a round that re-issues.

R63.name: shared_collection_race
R63.statement: Two deploys from one pre-state that both use the collection k race in check #1. The race is on the counter of k, or on the space counter when k has no counter yet. Any operations count: writes, removals, peeks and parks, because each one bumps the counter (decision 31).

R64.name: crossed_stacks_without_removal_counters_fabricate
R64.statement: Without the counter bump of the pops, checks #1 and #2 find nothing. No consume of the two logs names more than one channel, so check #3 has no join to see. Yet no serial order gives both branches their observations. After A, B pops 11 instead of 10, and after B, A pops 21 instead of 20.

R65.name: crossed_collections_race
R65.statement: Two branches that cross two collections, each writing one and removing from the other, race on both counters in check #1. The P5 property checks it for two stacks.

R66.name: unordered_writes_commute
R66.statement: Writes to collections without a counter touch no counter, never race in check #1, and merge into a state that both serial orders give. The P5 property checks it for the bag. The P5 property checks it for the bag, and the P6 property for the VectorDB family below its capacity.

V16.name: NoMergedOrderFabrication
V16.statement: With stacks (MC_CounterConflict_Stacks.cfg), a merge of two branches without a check #1 race is a serial run of whole deploys. RemovalCounterFreeUnsafe.cfg, whose pops do not bump the counter, refutes it.

R67.name: set_key_injective
R67.statement: The set key of two payloads is equal exactly when their canonical element encodings are equal. With an injective encode of sorted terms, the key is equal exactly when the sorted elements are equal (F5, F6).

R68.name: set_view_dedups_equal_pars
R68.statement: The view of a set holds one representative for each class: the first member in canonical order, independent of the list order. The first spatial match is a representative, and two records share a class exactly when their sorted payloads are equal (F7, decision 41).

R69.name: set_consume_retires_class
R69.statement: A receive that does not peek binds every stored member of the class of its choice, the representative first. Every member binds the pattern and passes the guard. The fire leaves no non-persistent member and keeps the persistent members and the other classes (F3, F8).

R70.name: set_retire_comm_lines_up
R70.statement: The consume over [D; n] of a class and every K_retire consume meet the staging rules of the substrate: one pattern for each channel, a canonical group, lined-up candidates, stored candidates, distinct claims. The class fire dispatches one result and a retire none (F9, F20).

R71.name: set_produce_fire_retires_stored_class
R71.statement: RETIRE-CLASS stages K_retire of each stored non-persistent member of the class of the element and changes no other record. In an offer, a fire of a waiter that does not peek leaves no non-persistent stored member of the class when the plan ends. An offer whose fired waiters all peek retires nothing (F10, decision 37).

R72.name: set_peek_restores_representative_only
R72.statement: A peek binds the representative alone. A persistent representative stays and nothing is sent again. Otherwise the fire removes it and RESTORE-SCAN sends it again, and when no waiter takes it the records are as before. A K_retire of the plan follows a fire of the second send on a waiter that does not peek, and then the class is cleared (decision 45, Rule E).

R73.name: set_membership_full_compare_on_equal_hash
R73.statement: The membership test answers key equality for every hash function, so a hash collision never makes two classes one. It compares the full keys exactly when the hashes are equal (DR-90).

R74.name: set_key_trace_covered
R74.statement: Every prefix of the trace of a set key and of a membership test reads at most what it reserved, so a cut budget rejects an operation before its commit (decision 42).

R75.name: pq_level_order
R75.statement: The levels form a total order in which the priority levels ascend. A receive binds the first level head, in this order, that its lane sees and whose payload matches its pattern (PqLevelOrder).

R76.name: pq_unprioritized_lowest
R76.statement: The unprioritized level comes after every priority level, so a receive binds an unprioritized record only when no visible head of a priority level matches its pattern (F6).

R77.name: pq_fifo_within_level
R77.statement: The head of each level and of each waiter queue is its entry with the least (ord, rank), and every fire of an operation, of a settle job and of a re-entry binds heads (FIFO, decision 11).

R78.name: pq_restricted_waiter_in_level_queue
R78.statement: A receive with priority p waits in the waiter queue of the level p, joins its tail, and fires only on the head of the level p (decision 38).

R79.name: pq_unrestricted_first_matching_level
R79.statement: An unrestricted receive binds the first level head, in ascending level order, whose payload matches its pattern. It checks its guard once on that head, and a refusal parks it (decision 38).

R80.name: pq_settle_oldest_first
R80.statement: Every fire of a settle fires the oldest fireable waiter-lane head (readiness review S4). A produce plan fires the older candidate head that fits its datum, and a refusal moves on (decisions 37 and 38).

R81.name: pq_settle_order_matters
R81.statement: Strict confluence fails: in the example S4, two fire orders end in two different states, and the settle stages the order that fires the oldest fireable head first.

R82.name: pq_produce_preserves_inv
R82.statement: A produce, fresh or re-entered, that completes in its round leaves INV: no head of a waiter lane can fire on the level heads that it sees.

R83.name: pq_consume_preserves_inv
R83.statement: A consume, fresh or re-entered, that completes in its round leaves INV.

R84.name: pq_head_blocks_within_level
R84.statement: For a cap above 0, a head that does not match blocks its lane: the receive parks and the send is stored, with no fire, although an entry behind a head may fit.

R85.name: pq_settle_terminates
R85.statement: A settle that starts after f fires of its transaction fires at most cap - f times and at most mu times, plus one divergent fire. Every transaction fires at most cap times, exactly cap times when it re-issues at the cap (I-21), and a settle job that completes leaves INV.

R86.name: pq_plan_permutation_invariant
R86.statement: Two views with the same entries in other list orders stage the same operations in a produce, a consume and a settle job, take the same next round, and reach views with the same entries.

R87.name: pq_without_settle_breaks_inv
R87.statement: Without the settle, two computed counterexamples (a fire exposes a waiter, and a fire exposes a record) break INV at the end of a completed operation. With the settle after the plan, INV holds.

R88.name: pq_priority_domain
R88.statement: A priority is admitted exactly when it is a natural number below the bound priorities of the space, when the space sets one. An admitted send runs at its level, and a send out of the domain fails before the bump and changes nothing.

R89.name: pq_no_level_storage
R89.statement: A level exists exactly when a record holds it, and an operation adds at most one entry to the view whatever its priority (I-10).

R90.name: pq_reissue_takes_level_fifo_place
R90.statement: A re-issued persistent send keeps its first-round order and takes its FIFO place in its level: behind an older head it is stored with no fire, and ahead of the head or on an empty level it plans. Every round bumps the one counter once.

R91.name: pq_reentered_waiter_keeps_seniority
R91.statement: A re-issued persistent receive keeps its first-round order and takes its FIFO place in its waiter queue, and it parks only itself, so the oldest-first rule ranks it with its first-round order.

R92.name: pq_peek_restores_head
R92.statement: A peek of a level head that is not persistent stores the record again at its order and level, the record is the head of its level again, and the settle after the plan stages nothing (Rule E).

R93.name: level_scan_trace_covered
R93.statement: The level scans of a priority queue reserve their reads before they make them (decision 42, DR-88): the trace of a transaction satisfies prefix coverage, with the reads after the commit.

R94.name: pq_settle_keeps_unspent_records
R94.statement: A settle loses no record: a stored record leaves the store only when a fire of a waiter that does not peek spends it, and a record in flight lands before a fire of a stored record, at the end and at a re-issue.

R95.name: datum_priority_slot_roundtrip
R95.statement: The priority slot of a datum record of a priority queue round-trips: GInt(p) for the level p >= 0 and Nil for the unprioritized level, and the decoder rejects every other slot.

R96.name: continuation_policy_slot_roundtrip
R96.statement: The policy slot of a continuation of a priority queue round-trips: EMap{"priority": GInt(p)} for the waiter queue of the level p and Nil for the unrestricted queue, and the outcome decoder accepts both.

V17.name: PqLevelOrder
V17.statement: Every fire binds the head of its lane and the head of its level, a receive and a settle bind the first matching level head that the lane sees, and a send precedes the stored records of its level, on every schedule.

V18.name: PqOldestFirst
V18.statement: Every fire of a settle fires the oldest fireable waiter-lane head, and every fire of a send fires the oldest candidate that fits, on every schedule.

V19.name: PqNoPendingMatch
V19.statement: With no round in progress, no element in flight and no settle job, no waiter-lane head can fire (INV), on every schedule.

V20.name: NoRecordLost
V20.statement: A record that was stored is stored, or in flight in the current settle, or a fire spent it, on every schedule.

V21.name: ReissueKeepsOrd
V21.statement: A re-issued persistent element carries the ord of its first round, and a re-issued element that is not persistent carries none, on every schedule (decision 43).

V22.name: TxnFiresBounded
V22.statement: No transaction makes more than Cap fires, its settles included (revision I-21), on every schedule.

R97.name: marker_record_roundtrip
R97.statement: The strict decoder of a path marker inverts its encoder, the encoder is injective, and the tag of a marker is the record tag of the kind I.

R98.name: vehicle_carries_payload
R98.statement: The vehicle of a datum on a prefix is the marker of the datum on that prefix followed by the payload, so its introduction bytes cover the payload (decision 40, Q3).

R99.name: path_element_rules
R99.statement: A path of more than 64 elements fails with PathTooDeep before the element scan, a PathMap or a zipper at any depth fails with UnsupportedPathElement, and the prefixes of an accepted path are closed and give at most 65 markers.

R100.name: delivery_vehicle_single_channel
R100.statement: Every event of a PathMap delivery is single-channel: the delivery COMM is on the index channel of the waiter, every retire is a single-channel K_retire, and the vehicle is never stored.

R101.name: prefix_contact_anchored
R101.statement: Every prefix contact of a stored datum and a waiter meets on the index channel of the prefix, because the datum has a marker there.

R102.name: peek_restores_delivered_marker
R102.statement: Under Rule E the second send of a peeked datum is offered most specific first, and it either restores the delivered marker with its identity or spends the datum.

R103.name: no_match_remains
R103.statement: The scan plans on prefixes leave no waiter without a guard that a stored datum under its prefix matches.

R104.name: marker_invariant_preserved
R104.statement: Every staging and every plan keeps the marker invariant: a stored datum on p has exactly one marker on I(q) for each prefix q of p, and no other marker exists.

R105.name: heads_no_match
R105.statement: On head-only disciplines over prefixes, the changed prefixes are covered, and a cascade ends with no fireable head.

R106.name: token_ord_reentry
R106.statement: The token gives distinct orders, a re-issued persistent operation keeps its first-round order, and a re-entry meets no tie (decisions 31 and 43).

R107.name: prefix_scan_trace_covered
R107.statement: The prefix scan reserves each unit of work before it reads, and the outcome after the commit reads nothing that the scan did not reserve (decision 42).

V23.name: NoMatchRemains
V23.statement: At every quiescent state of the PathMap bag model, no waiter without a guard matches a datum stored under its prefix.

V24.name: MarkerCount
V24.statement: Every stored datum has exactly one marker on the index channel of each prefix of its path, and every marker belongs to a stored datum.

V25.name: MergeDetectsPrefixContact
V25.statement: When two branches put a datum and a waiter on a path and a prefix of it, merge check #2 sees the contact on the shared index channel.

R108.name: join_search_is_head_greedy
R108.statement: The consume-side search of a join is GREEDY over the lane-visible windows in group order (HEAD's greedy, decision 37): sound, and the receive fires exactly when GREEDY succeeds and the guard admits the values in bind order once.

R109.name: join_produce_search_agrees_with_head
R109.statement: When GREEDY on the state with x stored binds x at p*, SEARCH-PRODUCE completes at a position p <= p* with that assignment at p*, and when HEAD's greedy (x at index 0) binds x both fire the same assignment.

R110.name: join_incoming_binds_once
R110.statement: Every produce-side join fire binds its incoming record at exactly one position, after at most m_W(c_x) attempts (decision 28).

R111.name: join_fires_heads_only
R111.statement: Every fire of the join engine (OFFER, RECEIVE, the cascade) is at the head of each lane of every collection of its group and binds records of its windows.

R112.name: join_repeated_channel_distinct_records
R112.statement: The binds of one fire bind pairwise distinct records (distinct classes for a set), persistent records included.

R113.name: join_set_bind_retires_class
R113.statement: After a set fire whose waiter does not peek (a produce-side, consume-side or cascade fire), no non-persistent member of a bound class stays stored, and a peek fire retires nothing.

R114.name: cascade_terminates
R114.statement: Each step of DRAIN-AND-CASCADE that goes on lowers mu lexicographically or stops, also when the persistent element of the operation is a pending second send (DV-3), and a drain that starts after f fires stages at most cap - f fires.

R115.name: join_txn_fires_bounded
R115.statement: The settle before the plan, the plan, the second sends and the cascade share one fire count (decision 49): a transaction makes at most FIRE_ROUND_CAP fires, and a settle job starts at 0.

R116.name: cascade_restores_inv
R116.statement: The head-only disciplines (decision 11) and the set (decision 50): every fireable waiter at the end of a transaction has a dirty collection (CI), and a transaction with no stop ends with no work and INV_head (no waiter is fireable, guarded waiters included). Bag: INV_scan holds at the end of every transaction. Without the set cascade, a class move breaks INV_scan (set_join_class_shift_breaks_inv_scan).

R117.name: cascade_order_independent
R117.statement: Single-head disciplines: two fireable waiters that do not peek have disjoint groups, each stays fireable after the fire of the other, and the two fires commute.

R118.name: lift_reoffer_equals_direct_comm
R118.statement: Lift and re-offer leave the view of one direct COMM of the stored pair and add only the K_lift events after the bumps of TOUCH, and the K_retire events of a set fire that does not peek (decision 50).

R119.name: cascade_bumps_touched_counters
R119.statement: For a discipline with a counter, every staging of a transaction on a collection follows the one bump of its counter in that transaction.

R120.name: bind_permutation_restores_order
R120.statement: The canonical group order is a function of the bind multiset (FR-1'), and the v2 slots put the receipt results back in bind order for every permutation.

R121.name: plan_then_lock_stable
R121.statement: Every staging of RUN-JOIN lies in the lock keys of the join closure; with the footprint premise PREPARE runs the plan of the state once and its lock check passes.

R122.name: join_reissue_keeps_bind_ords
R122.statement: A re-issued persistent JoinOp carries its first-round ords (one for each bind), and each round bumps every own counter (decision 43).

R123.name: peek_join_restores_stored_candidates
R123.statement: A peek join fire sends every removed non-persistent record again through OFFER, in receipt order, with its own identity and authority, and the element in flight also when it is persistent (decision 30, DV-3). No record is lost, also across a stop. At a stop the element of the operation returns to its operation, and a stop that owes nothing re-issues its resume only (DV-5).

R124.name: greedy_join_can_miss_assignment
R124.statement: A computed negative result: on a repeated channel, GREEDY parks a waiter although an assignment exists (decision 37 until P12).

R125.name: continuation_v2_roundtrip
R125.statement: The version 2 continuation record of a join waiter decodes back to its slots and its continuation; every version 1 decoder rejects it, and the version 2 decoder rejects the version 1 records (each compares the whole tag).

R126.name: join_ops_race_on_every_counter
R126.statement: A join step over ks and any step on a collection k of ks, from one pre-state, race in check #1 on the counter of k, or on the space counter when k is new.

V26.name: QuiescentNoPendingMatch
V26.statement: With no re-issued operation and no settle job outstanding, no waiter is fireable (queue, stack and set) and no waiter without a guard has a greedy match (bag).

V27.name: JoinFiresHeadsOnly
V27.statement: Every fire of the join engine is at the head of each collection of its group.

V28.name: DistinctRecordsPerBind
V28.statement: The stored records of one fire are pairwise distinct, and of distinct classes on a set.

V29.name: IncomingBoundOnce
V29.statement: A produce-side fire binds its incoming record at exactly one position.

V30.name: CascadeMeasureDecreases
V30.statement: Each drain step that goes on lowers mu or stops.

V31.name: TxnFiresBounded
V31.statement: No join transaction makes more than Cap fires.

V32.name: NoRecordLost
V32.statement: Every record that a transaction holds is stored, spent by a fire of a waiter that does not peek or by a retirement, or pending in an outstanding settle job.

V33.name: ReissueKeepsBindOrds
V33.statement: A re-issued persistent operation carries the ords of its first round, and another re-issued operation carries none.

V34.name: TouchedCountersBumped
V34.statement: Each staging of a join transaction on a collection follows a bump of its counter in the same transaction (queue, stack).

R127.name: set_retirements_race
R127.statement: Two branches from one pre-state that each retire one stored member of a set, by the class fire over [D; n] or by a K_retire COMM, race in check #1 on the channel of the member (F24 of the P5 design v2).

R128.name: unordered_set_writes_commute
R128.statement: Writes to set collections merge with no race, and every view of a set that ignores the order of its records, as the class view in the canonical order of DR-75 does, gives the merged records the view of both serial orders (F25 of the P5 design v2).

R129.name: pathmap_token_race
R129.statement: Two branches that each run a PathMap step that bumps the token of one space race on S(sid) in check #1. A step bumps the token when its discipline is ordered, or when its transaction changes the state (decision 51).

R130.name: vectordb_params_validated
R130.statement: P6: exactly the VectorDB families hashmap:vectordb and vector:vectordb take capacity, dimensions, metric and mirror, and they require capacity and dimensions; every other family refuses the four names. capacity accepts exactly the GInt values in [1, 1000000], dimensions the GInt values in [1, 4096], metric the six metric names and mirror the name chroma. A missing capacity, then a missing dimensions, fails with MissingParam. Gate 9 runs on the canonical params and accepts a mirror exactly with the default qualifier and a metric (cosine without the param) that ChromaDB indexes: cosine, dot or euclidean.

R131.name: capped_writes_soft_bound
R131.statement: Decision 71: two branches of capped stores (a VectorDB collection) that both pass from one base merge without a race in check #1. The merge holds the base records and both branches' stores, so it can exceed the capacity, by at most the stores of the branch with fewer stores. The serial order passes exactly when the stores of both fit, and a store fails exactly on a collection that holds the capacity or more.

D47.title: Decision 47: spaces in native execution: the native replay backend (EventCorrelation.v H24-H26, NativeReplay.tla T8), the view charges (EventCorrelation.v H27, P5 of design v2) and the scheduling of space intents (NativeReplay.tla NoBlockedReadiness and NoDeadlock).
D47.design: Decision 47 design v2, section 5, and the epoch closure of commit c6cb371ba. witness_tests lists the deterministic tests of section 6.

N1.name: native_replay_reproduces_play
N1.statement: Native replay over the journal rows of native play makes the observer calls of play in the order of play, applies the effects of play and ends with the status of play. Play records at most one row for each operation, and one row for each operation when it completes (H24).

N2.name: native_replay_denial_keeps_prefix
N2.statement: When play runs out of phlo at operation k, play keeps the effects of the operations before k and records k + 1 rows, and native replay over those rows ends with the same calls, the same store and OutOfPhlogistons (H25).

N3.name: native_replay_fails_closed
N3.statement: Native replay fails closed before any effect: no ready row ends NotReady with no call, a forged footprint and an outcome that does not fit the staged kind end Mismatch before any call, and a fire whose recorded candidate is another COMM ends Mismatch after its introduction only, with no COMM observation and no effect (H26).

N4.name: view_charge_cache_independent
N4.statement: A view load charges its key and its value only: a hit and a miss load the same value and charge the same amount, so a warm load and a cold load reserve the same work (H27, P5 of design v2).

N5.name: NativeReplayOutcomeEqual
N5.statement: T8: native replay accepts the journal of play, and only it, and then it has the observer calls, the spending, the effects and the status of play, for every transaction of up to three stores and fires, every phlo limit up to 6 and every journal with one tampered well-formed row.

N6.name: NoBlockedReadiness
N6.statement: With an honest journal, no space row finds a predecessor that is not complete: the key [2]||sid (I-11) keeps the transactions of one space in one conflict group in operation order, also without the native key [2, 0].

N7.name: NoDeadlock
N7.statement: Until every intent ends, some intent can step: a space transaction never waits under its stripes (P1), a host operation waits before it takes its stripes (F4), and a failed space row closes the epoch, so no operation waits forever for it, also with a footprint-consistent forged journal.

P6.title: P6 steps 2, 8b, 8c and 8d: the exact numeric core of the VectorDB family (Similarity.v S1-S20: the squared forms, the bounds, the kernel laws, Cauchy-Schwarz, the score orders, the binary metrics and the selection order with the kappa tie-break), the VectorDB discipline of one collection (VectorDbDiscipline.v S21-S25) the replay of its transactions (S26, the H23 theorem of EventCorrelation.v), and its TLA+ model VectorDb.tla (W1-W4: no pending match, atomic list fires, conservation of peeked records, the measure of the tail), the replies of rho:lang:vector (VectorOps.v S27-S28: the widest kind with one rounding, the midpoint test of the nearest root), and the ChromaDB mirror of a VectorDB space (ChromaMirror.tla W5-W12: consensus independent of the mirror, recorded answers, the checks of ann in both modes, publication on success with exact net writes and no wait, and the reconciler).

S1.name: cosine_squared_form_iff
S1.statement: In every ordered commutative ring, the real numbers included: for s = |q|·|e| > 0, t·s ≤ q·e (cos ≥ t) holds exactly when cosine_within(q·e, t, s·s), the decision of within, which uses no root.

S2.name: cosine_order_squared_form
S2.statement: With s_i·s_i = |q|²·|e_i|², the real order cos_1 ≤ cos_2 holds exactly when cosine_le, the order of better, which cross-multiplies the squares by the norms of the other record.

S3.name: euclidean_radius_squared_form
S3.statement: For a distance d ≥ 0, d ≤ r holds exactly when euclidean_within(d², r): r ≥ 0 and d² ≤ r².

S4.name: threshold_monotone
S4.statement: A lower threshold admits every record that a higher threshold admits, under cosine, dot and jaccard.

S5.name: radius_monotone
S5.statement: A larger radius admits every record that a smaller radius admits, under euclidean, manhattan and hamming.

S6.name: dot_laws
S6.statement: The dot product is symmetric, and its exact sum does not depend on the order of the coordinates.

S7.name: distance_laws
S7.statement: dist2 is non-negative, symmetric and zero exactly on equal vectors; manhattan is non-negative, symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality.

S9.name: cosine_bounds
S9.statement: Every record passes the cosine threshold −1, and no record passes a threshold above 1.

S10.name: score_orders_total
S10.statement: The order of each of the six metrics is a total preorder on its scores: cosine over positive record norms, dot and the distances by their values, jaccard over positive unions.

S11.name: squared_forms_embed
S11.statement: An embedding of ordered rings keeps the decisions of S1 to S3, so the decisions in the rationals are the decisions in the real numbers.

S12.name: binary_laws
S12.statement: Hamming is a metric on binary vectors, the jaccard counts satisfy inter ≤ union and are symmetric, and the union is empty only when neither vector sets a position.

S13.name: selection_total_order
S13.statement: The selection order (the better score, then the lower DR-75 rank) is irreflexive, transitive and total on distinct ranks.

S14.name: topk_deterministic
S14.statement: Two sorted arrangements of one multiset of candidates are equal, so their first k candidates are equal.

S15.name: list_selection_deterministic
S15.statement: List mode, the first k eligible candidates in the selection order, depends only on the multiset of records, and the insertion sort computes it.

S16.name: kappa_dropped_not_unique
S16.statement: Negative control: by score alone, two equal-score records have two sorted arrangements with different first records.

S17.name: Qc_ordered_ring
S17.statement: The canonical rationals satisfy every hypothesis of the ordered ring of Part 1.

S18.name: similarity_headlines_Qc
S18.statement: S1, S2, S3, S8 and S9 hold in the canonical rationals.

S19.name: squared_forms_embed_Z_Qc
S19.statement: S11 holds for the embedding of the integers into the rationals.

S20.name: selection_Qc
S20.statement: S13 and S14 hold for rational scores.

S21.name: vdb_join_removal_exposes_nothing
S21.statement: A removal keeps the order of each similarity window, so a greedy search of single-mode binds that fails before a removal fails after it. The search of one bind is the selection of the driver (design v3 4.6).

S22.name: vdb_no_pending_match
S22.statement: A transaction that ends leaves no parked waiter without a guard that can fire, in single mode and in list mode (LM-b, decision 66).

S23.name: vdb_list_needs_cascade
S23.statement: Negative result, computed: without LIST-CASCADE a receive ends with a parked list waiter that can fire (the counterexample CE-2 of the arbitration).

S24.name: vdb_txn_bounded
S24.statement: For a cap above 0, a transaction makes at most cap fires, and each loop of RECEIVE-VDB, OFFER-VDB and the tail ends within the fuel that the plans compute (I-21, decision 49).

S25.name: vdb_no_record_lost
S25.statement: Rule E (decision 45): a record of the pre-state is in the post-state of a transaction that ends, or a fire of a waiter that does not peek spent it.

S26.name: replay_reproduces_play_run
S26.statement: Replay stages the operations of play, pairs each recorded COMM once, and reproduces the run of play: its observer calls, its effects and its status (H23, decision 36). The VectorDB plans stage through the substrate, so their transactions replay this way.

W1.name: QuiescentNoPendingMatch
W1.statement: With no re-issued operation and no settle job outstanding, no parked waiter can fire on the records, for every schedule of the bounded configurations, with settle jobs and re-issues at the round cap (LM-b).

W2.name: ListAtomic
W2.statement: A list fire of a waiter that does not peek spends each member of its list that is not persistent, in the transaction of the fire (K_retire and K_lift).

W3.name: PeekConservation
W3.statement: Every record that was stored is stored, spent by a fire of a waiter that does not peek, or pending in an outstanding settle job (Rule E, decisions 30 and 45).

W4.name: CascadeTerminates
W4.statement: Each step of each tail lowers the measure 2 * (Cap - fired) + |owed| or stops the transaction, and no transaction runs out of its fuel (decision 49, I-21).

S27.name: vector_replies_exact
S27.statement: The reply of add, scale and dot has the widest kind of the inputs. It is the exact value for the integer and the rational kinds, and one rounding of the exact value for the float kind: dot rounds its exact sum once (decisions 54 and 66).

S28.name: root_midpoint_nearest
S28.statement: When the squares of the midpoints between a representable reply r and its neighbours bound x = s * s with s >= 0, no representable value is nearer to s than r: the check of the correctly rounded roots of norm and distance.

W5.name: ConsensusIndependentOfMirror
W5.statement: The post-state of each deploy is a function of its pre-state and its recorded answer only: no mirror write runs in a transaction (design v3 4.9).

W6.name: AdvisoryRecorded
W6.statement: Replay uses the recorded answer of ann and never asks its own mirror (decision 57).

W7.name: EqualHostWork
W7.statement: Play and replay make the same checks of an ann call, so they reserve the same host work for them (decision 67).

W8.name: PublishOnlyOnSuccess
W8.statement: Every published write comes from a deploy whose final result has no errors, and the clear at the start of a root evaluation drops the journal of an exploratory evaluation (M1, decision 66).

W9.name: NetWritesExact
W9.statement: A published batch upserts exactly the records that its deploy added and deletes exactly the records that it removed, so a Rule E pair writes nothing.

W10.name: PublishNeverWaits
W10.statement: A publication never waits for the writer: a full queue marks the collection dirty (decision 58).

W11.name: ReconciledEqualsFinalizedView
W11.statement: After a reconciler pass that finishes, the mirror holds the finalized view on every registered channel (decision 66).

W12.name: WatermarkHonest
W12.statement: The watermark of a collection never passes the block of the last reconciler pass that finished.

The witness tests of W5 are in reified_theory.rs and in the library tests of spaces/theory, spaces/generic.rs and spaces/factory/constructor.rs. V1.name: sweep_complete
V1.statement: When the lock keys of every transaction of a root evaluation cover the channels that it stages (readiness review S2), the book of the evaluation holds every staged volatile channel, and the sweep of the book leaves no record, no join entry and no waiting continuation on them (design v3 VR-2).

V2.name: dead_ephemeral_dangling
V2.statement: The spaces of two deploys are disjoint (I-19), so a space of another deploy is never live in this evaluation, and the live check passes exactly the spaces that this evaluation created (design v3 DG-1).

V3.name: seq_name_iff
V3.statement: The name of a space is a seq name exactly when its space is a live ephemeral space that is not exempt, and the handle of a space and the names of a durable space are never seq names (design v3 SQ-1).

V4.name: SeqExclusive
V4.statement: For each channel of a seq space, the admitted uses form one prefix chain of participant paths (design v3 SQ-3, SQ-4, decision 73).

V5.name: SeqNotSent
V5.statement: No delivered message holds a seq name (design v3 SQ-2).

V6.name: QualifierSupport
V6.statement: Gate 3 creates a HashSet space only with seq, and a seq space only in native execution (design v3 QT-4, QT-5).

V7.name: UseBalance
V7.statement: The use context of each participant is its lexical context.

V8.name: ClaimTracksLastUse
V8.statement: The claim of a channel of a seq space is its last admitted use (design v3 SQ-4).

V9.name: hashset_unit_rules
V9.statement: The payload check of a HashSet collection accepts exactly the empty payload and its pattern check exactly the empty pattern list with no binder and no remainder. An empty pattern list matches exactly the empty payload, a rejected send or receive stages nothing, and so every record of a HashSet store is a unit (design v3 HS-2, HS-3, HS-5).

V10.name: builtin_decidable_structural
V10.statement: With a limit of at least one unit, each builtin decides every value by its shape as TH-1 states, never Undetermined, with the usage {1, 0} and one reserved unit; a match checks every stored value for one unit; a limit of 0 gives Undetermined before any reservation (design v3 TH-1, TH-8).

V11.name: fail_closed
V11.statement: A send is admitted exactly when every value is Proven; otherwise it aborts at its first value that is not, with TheoryRefuted or TheoryUndetermined and its index; a commit with two or more leases is refused (design v3 TH-5, TH-9).

V12.name: usage_cache_transparent
V12.statement: A cache whose entries are results of the check gives the verdict and the reserved units of the check on a hit and a miss, and stays consistent (design v3 TH-8).

V13.name: resolve_identity_deterministic
V13.statement: The resolution is a function of the content of the identity: exactly the structural builtins resolve, with any limit profile, and every identity that the factory builds resolves to its kind (design v3 TH-2, TH-3).

V14.name: replay_preserves_theory_admission
V14.statement: Replay decodes the persisted identity bytes and admits or refuses each send as play does, at the same index and with the same reserved units; an identity that names no checker fails the send (design v3 TH-5, TH-7, TH-8).

V15.name: identity_bytes_roundtrip
V15.statement: The decoder of the identity bytes inverts the encoder, accepts only the image of the encoder, and the encoder is injective (decision 74).

V16.name: theory_refusal_is_guard_refusal
V16.statement: The theory of the space at a match is part of the guard: a fire binds a stored record that the guard and the theory admit, a theory refusal is a guard refusal, a refused first match parks, a theory that proves every datum changes no choice, and a datum in flight is never checked (design v3 TH-6).

V17.name: theory_gate_validated
V17.statement: Gate 4 passes no theory and the builtin names without arguments; a builtin with arguments fails with BadConstructorArgument, another name with UnknownTheory and the least builtin within two edits; gate 4 runs after gate 3 and before the params gates (design v3 TH-4).

V18.name: view_charge_cache_independent
V18.statement: A view load charges its key and its value only, so a warm load and a cold load reserve the same work (H27 of decision 47, rule NE-2). No Reified state outlives an evaluation (F18), so the first operation on a space after a restart reads the keys and the values of a warm runtime and pays the same: the outcome and the cost vector are equal (design v3 RH-1 and RH-4).

A1.name: agent_ref_requires_write_flag
A1.statement: A use block enters the context of a user agent exactly when the evaluated reference has a call channel under the bundle rule of eval_send; under a bundle without the write flag it fails with HandleNotWritable.

A2.name: r7_agent_reply_bundle_exact
A2.statement: For every single bundle, the R7 backend makes the call on a user agent exactly when the bundle has both flags and its body is an agent-tagged tuple, with the agent and the raw channel of the tuple; every other bundle routes to the default space, as in HEAD (R7A-1).

A3.name: offsets_partition
A3.statement: The ranges [off_i, off_i + f_i) of the binds of a translated receive partition the binder positions [0, total): every position below total has exactly one owner bind (TR-3).

A4.name: env_keys_disjoint_union
A4.statement: The env keys of the binds of a translated receive are disjoint, and their union is the key set {0, ..., total - 1} of the map pattern of the body receive (MO-3, TR-6).

A5.name: body_equivalence
A5.statement: The body receive binds, in binder order, exactly the values that the native receive binds: the matched values of every bind in bind order (TR-6).

A6.name: guard_fold_sound
A6.statement: The guard of the owner bind of TR-4, over the placeholders of that bind, has the value of the native guard over the values of every bind, so the matcher filters as the native guard check does.

A7.name: matcher_sound_complete
A7.statement: The matcher op replies (true, env) exactly when the spatial match of the injected matcher succeeds and the guard of the bind passes, and env maps the global position of each binder of the bind to its value (MO-3).

A8.name: matcher_state_roundtrip
A8.statement: The codec of a matcher state is exact: a consistent state decodes from its encoding and from its matcher id, a decoded state re-encodes to the same bytes, and the encoding is injective (TR-5, MO-2).

A9.name: tag_untag_id
A9.statement: An agent-minted name is one bundle with both flags around the agent-tagged tuple of its agent and its raw channel: the write rule of eval_send and the read rule of unbundle_receive both give the tuple, the tuple routes to its agent with its raw channel under every context (R4), and the R7 backend reads the same agent and raw channel from the name (R7A-1), whatever the bit sets are (TN-3).

A10.name: resume_binds_innermost
A10.statement: The resume term of a translated new binds every binder of the new in its order: inside the nested receives, which bind one reply per agent binder in agent-binder order, each target evaluates to the bound name of its binder or to the agent-minted name of the reply of its rank, and the match pushes the values so that BoundVar(k - 1 - j) reads binder j, as in a native new (TN-3).

A11.name: RoutingIsolation
A11.statement: Under every use-context, also the context of an agent, a name of a native space routes to that space and an agent-minted name routes to its agent, so no call of an agent carries a name of another space (R3, R4).

A12.name: SystemChannelsDefault
A12.statement: Under every use-context, also the context of an agent, system channels, default objects and other unforgeable names route to the default space, so no call of an agent carries one (R1).

A13.name: JoinSameSpace
A13.statement: A receive aborts with CrossSpaceJoin exactly when its binds route to two spaces, and a receive whose binds route to one space runs on that space (TR-1).

A14.name: HandleUnwrapExact
A14.statement: A space reference names a space exactly when it is bare or under one bundle with the write flag, and the space is the unwrapped reference (AG-4).

A15.name: ReplayEquivalence
A15.statement: Each call and each send of an agent is an ordinary event of the default space, so the replay of the call log gives the state of the agent, its sends and the runs of each body, also for an agent that breaks its obligations.

A16.name: BodyAtMostOnceLinear
A16.statement: The body receive of a translated receive is persistent only for <=, so the body of a linear receive runs at most once, also when the agent sends to it again (TR-6, ASO-2).

A17.name: NoMatchRemains
A17.statement: The reference agent keeps no stored consume whose matchers accept distinct stored messages after a method completes (ASO-1); a faulty agent that stores a consume without a try breaks it.
